passages.text: “Now you, son of man, take a brick, place it before you, and draw on it the city of Jerusalem.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Ezekiel.
Ezekiel was a prophet.
God called Ezekiel “son of man.”
God gave Ezekiel a command.
God told Ezekiel to take a brick.
God told Ezekiel to place the brick in front of himself.
God told Ezekiel to draw a city on the brick.
God told Ezekiel to draw Jerusalem on the brick.
passages.original: וְאַתָּ֤ה בֶן־ אָדָם֙ קַח־ לְךָ֣ לְבֵנָ֔ה וְנָתַתָּ֥ה אוֹתָ֖הּ לְפָנֶ֑יךָ וְחַקּוֹתָ֥ עָלֶ֛יהָ עִ֖יר אֶת־ יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם׃

passages.text: Then lay siege against it: Construct a siege wall, build a ramp to it, set up camps against it, and place battering rams around it on all sides.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Ezekiel, the prophet.
God told Ezekiel to act out a message for Israel.
God told Ezekiel to lay siege against the model of Jerusalem.
Ezekiel must build a siege wall against the city.
Ezekiel must build a ramp up to the city.
Ezekiel must set up camps against the city.
Ezekiel must place battering rams around the city on every side.
passages.original: וְנָתַתָּ֨ה עָלֶ֜יהָ מָצ֗וֹר וּבָנִ֤יתָ עָלֶ֙יהָ֙ דָּיֵ֔ק וְשָׁפַכְתָּ֥ עָלֶ֖יהָ סֹֽלְלָ֑ה וְנָתַתָּ֨ה עָלֶ֧יהָ מַחֲנ֛וֹת וְשִׂים־ עָלֶ֥יהָ כָּרִ֖ים סָבִֽיב׃

passages.text: Then take an iron plate and set it up as an iron wall between yourself and the city. Turn your face toward it so that it is under siege, and besiege it. This will be a sign to the house of Israel.
passages.sermon:
Ezekiel was a prophet.
God spoke to Ezekiel.
God called Ezekiel "son of man."
God gave Ezekiel a command.
God told Ezekiel to take an iron plate.
Ezekiel must set the iron plate up as a wall.
The iron wall must stand between Ezekiel and the city.
The city is Jerusalem.
Ezekiel must turn his face toward the city.
Ezekiel must act as if the city is under siege.
Ezekiel must besiege the city.
This action will be a sign.
The sign is for the house of Israel.
passages.original: וְאַתָּ֤ה קַח־ לְךָ֙ מַחֲבַ֣ת בַּרְזֶ֔ל וְנָתַתָּ֤ה אוֹתָהּ֙ קִ֣יר בַּרְזֶ֔ל בֵּינְךָ֖ וּבֵ֣ין הָעִ֑יר וַהֲכִינֹתָה֩ אֶת־ פָּנֶ֨יךָ אֵלֶ֜יהָ וְהָיְתָ֤ה בַמָּצוֹר֙ וְצַרְתָּ֣ עָלֶ֔יהָ א֥וֹת הִ֖יא לְבֵ֥ית יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃ס

passages.text: Then lie down on your left side and place the iniquity of the house of Israel upon yourself. You are to bear their iniquity for the number of days you lie on your side.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Ezekiel the prophet.
God commanded Ezekiel to lie down on his left side.
Ezekiel must place the sin of the house of Israel upon himself.
Ezekiel must do this for a set number of days.
Ezekiel will bear the iniquity of the house of Israel for each day he lies on his side.
passages.original: וְאַתָּ֤ה שְׁכַב֙ עַל־ צִדְּךָ֣ הַשְּׂמָאלִ֔י וְשַׂמְתָּ֛ אֶת־ עֲוֺ֥ן בֵּֽית־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל עָלָ֑יו מִסְפַּ֤ר הַיָּמִים֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר תִּשְׁכַּ֣ב עָלָ֔יו תִּשָּׂ֖א אֶת־ עֲוֺנָֽם׃

passages.text: For I have assigned to you 390 days, according to the number of years of their iniquity. So you shall bear the iniquity of the house of Israel.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Ezekiel.
God gave Ezekiel a task.
God assigned Ezekiel 390 days.
This number matches the years of Israel’s sin.
Ezekiel must bear the iniquity of the house of Israel.
passages.original: וַאֲנִ֗י נָתַ֤תִּֽי לְךָ֙ אֶת־ שְׁנֵ֣י עֲוֺנָ֔ם לְמִסְפַּ֣ר יָמִ֔ים שְׁלֹשׁ־ מֵא֥וֹת וְתִשְׁעִ֖ים י֑וֹם וְנָשָׂ֖אתָ עֲוֺ֥ן בֵּֽית־ יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

passages.text: When you have completed these days, lie down again, but on your right side, and bear the iniquity of the house of Judah. I have assigned to you 40 days, a day for each year.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Ezekiel.
God gave Ezekiel a command.
Ezekiel must finish the first period of lying on his left side.
After this, Ezekiel must lie down again.
This time, Ezekiel must lie on his right side.
Ezekiel must bear the iniquity of the house of Judah.
God assigned Ezekiel forty days for this task.
Each day represents one year of Judah’s iniquity.
passages.original: וְכִלִּיתָ֣ אֶת־ אֵ֗לֶּה וְשָׁ֨כַבְתָּ֜ עַל־ צִדְּךָ֤ הַיְמוֹנִי שֵׁנִ֔ית וְנָשָׂ֖אתָ אֶת־ עֲוֺ֣ן בֵּית־ יְהוּדָ֑ה אַרְבָּעִ֣ים י֔וֹם י֧וֹם לַשָּׁנָ֛ה י֥וֹם לַשָּׁנָ֖ה נְתַתִּ֥יו לָֽךְ׃

passages.text: You must turn your face toward the siege of Jerusalem with your arm bared, and prophesy against it.
passages.sermon:
Ezekiel was a prophet.
God gave Ezekiel a command.
Ezekiel must turn his face toward the siege of Jerusalem.
Ezekiel must bare his arm.
Ezekiel must prophesy against Jerusalem.
passages.original: וְאֶל־ מְצ֤וֹר יְרוּשָׁלִַ֙ם֙ תָּכִ֣ין פָּנֶ֔יךָ וּֽזְרֹעֲךָ֖ חֲשׂוּפָ֑ה וְנִבֵּאתָ֖ עָלֶֽיהָ׃

passages.text: Now behold, I will tie you up with ropes so you cannot turn from side to side until you have finished the days of your siege.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Ezekiel.
God said, “I will tie you up with ropes.
You will not turn from one side to the other.
You must stay like this until you finish the days of your siege.”
passages.original: וְהִנֵּ֛ה נָתַ֥תִּי עָלֶ֖יךָ עֲבוֹתִ֑ים וְלֹֽא־ תֵהָפֵ֤ךְ מִֽצִּדְּךָ֙ אֶל־ צִדֶּ֔ךָ עַד־ כַּלּוֹתְךָ֖ יְמֵ֥י מְצוּרֶֽךָ׃

passages.text: But take wheat, barley, beans, lentils, millet, and spelt; put them in a single container and make them into bread for yourself. This is what you are to eat during the 390 days you lie on your side.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Ezekiel.
God told Ezekiel to take wheat, barley, beans, lentils, millet, and spelt.
God told Ezekiel to put all these foods in one container.
God told Ezekiel to make bread from these foods for himself.
God told Ezekiel to eat this bread.
God told Ezekiel to eat this bread during the 390 days he would lie on his side.
passages.original: וְאַתָּ֣ה קַח־ לְךָ֡ חִטִּ֡ין וּ֠שְׂעֹרִים וּפ֨וֹל וַעֲדָשִׁ֜ים וְדֹ֣חַן וְכֻסְּמִ֗ים וְנָתַתָּ֤ה אוֹתָם֙ בִּכְלִ֣י אֶחָ֔ד וְעָשִׂ֧יתָ אוֹתָ֛ם לְךָ֖ לְלָ֑חֶם מִסְפַּ֨ר הַיָּמִ֜ים אֲשֶׁר־ אַתָּ֣ה׀ שׁוֹכֵ֣ב עַֽל־ צִדְּךָ֗ שְׁלֹשׁ־ מֵא֧וֹת וְתִשְׁעִ֛ים י֖וֹם תֹּאכֲלֶֽנּוּ׃

passages.text: You are to weigh out twenty shekels of food to eat each day, and you are to eat it at set times.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Ezekiel.
God gave Ezekiel a command.
Ezekiel must eat food each day.
Ezekiel must weigh the food.
The food must weigh twenty shekels each day.
Ezekiel must eat the food at set times.
passages.original: וּמַאֲכָֽלְךָ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר תֹּאכֲלֶ֔נּוּ בְּמִשְׁק֕וֹל עֶשְׂרִ֥ים שֶׁ֖קֶל לַיּ֑וֹם מֵעֵ֥ת עַד־ עֵ֖ת תֹּאכֲלֶֽנּוּ׃

passages.text: You are also to measure out a sixth of a hin of water to drink, and you are to drink it at set times.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Ezekiel.
God gave Ezekiel a command.
God told Ezekiel to drink water.
Ezekiel must measure the water.
Ezekiel must take one sixth of a hin of water.
Ezekiel must drink only this amount.
Ezekiel must drink the water at set times.
passages.original: וּמַ֛יִם בִּמְשׂוּרָ֥ה תִשְׁתֶּ֖ה שִׁשִּׁ֣ית הַהִ֑ין מֵעֵ֥ת עַד־ עֵ֖ת תִּשְׁתֶּֽה׃

passages.text: And you shall eat the food as you would a barley cake, after you bake it over dried human excrement in the sight of the people.”
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Ezekiel.
God gave Ezekiel a command.
Ezekiel must eat his food as a barley cake.
Ezekiel must bake this food over dried human excrement.
Ezekiel must do this where the people can see him.
passages.original: וְעֻגַ֥ת שְׂעֹרִ֖ים תֹּֽאכֲלֶ֑נָּה וְהִ֗יא בְּגֶֽלְלֵי֙ צֵאַ֣ת הָֽאָדָ֔ם תְּעֻגֶ֖נָה לְעֵינֵיהֶֽם׃ס

passages.text: Then the LORD said, “This is how the Israelites will eat their defiled bread among the nations to which I will banish them.”
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke.
The LORD described the future of the Israelites.
The LORD said the Israelites will eat bread.
Their bread will be defiled.
The Israelites will eat this bread among foreign nations.
The LORD will banish the Israelites to these nations.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יְהוָ֔ה כָּ֣כָה יֹאכְל֧וּ בְנֵֽי־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל אֶת־ לַחְמָ֖ם טָמֵ֑א בַּגּוֹיִ֕ם אֲשֶׁ֥ר אַדִּיחֵ֖ם שָֽׁם׃

passages.text: “Ah, Lord GOD,” I said, “I have never defiled myself. From my youth until now I have not eaten anything found dead or mauled by wild beasts. No unclean meat has ever entered my mouth.”
passages.sermon:
Ezekiel was a prophet of God.
Ezekiel spoke to the Lord God.
Ezekiel said, “Ah, Lord God.
I have never defiled myself.
From my youth until now, I have not eaten anything found dead.
I have not eaten anything killed by wild beasts.
No unclean meat has ever entered my mouth.”
passages.original: וָאֹמַ֗ר אֲהָהּ֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה הִנֵּ֥ה נַפְשִׁ֖י לֹ֣א מְטֻמָּאָ֑ה וּנְבֵלָ֨ה וּטְרֵפָ֤ה לֹֽא־ אָכַ֙לְתִּי֙ מִנְּעוּרַ֣י וְעַד־ עַ֔תָּה וְלֹא־ בָ֥א בְּפִ֖י בְּשַׂ֥ר פִּגּֽוּל׃ס

passages.text: “Look,” He replied, “I will let you use cow dung instead of human excrement, and you may bake your bread over that.”
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Ezekiel.
God said, “Look at what I am giving you now.
I am giving you cow dung.
You will use cow dung instead of human excrement.
You will bake your bread over cow dung.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלַ֔י רְאֵ֗ה נָתַ֤תִּֽי לְךָ֙ אֶת־ צְפוּעֵי הַבָּקָ֔ר תַּ֖חַת גֶּלְלֵ֣י הָֽאָדָ֑ם וְעָשִׂ֥יתָ אֶֽת־ לַחְמְךָ֖ עֲלֵיהֶֽם׃ס

passages.text: Then He told me, “Son of man, I am going to cut off the supply of food in Jerusalem. They will anxiously eat bread rationed by weight, and in despair they will drink water by measure.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Ezekiel.
God called Ezekiel “son of man.”
God said He would cut off the supply of food in Jerusalem.
The people in Jerusalem would eat bread in small, measured amounts.
They would feel anxious as they ate.
They would drink water in limited, measured amounts.
They would feel despair as they drank.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלַ֗י בֶּן־ אָדָם֙ הִנְנִ֨י שֹׁבֵ֤ר מַטֵּה־ לֶ֙חֶם֙ בִּיר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם וְאָכְלוּ־ לֶ֥חֶם בְּמִשְׁקָ֖ל וּבִדְאָגָ֑ה וּמַ֕יִם בִּמְשׂוּרָ֥ה וּבְשִׁמָּמ֖וֹן יִשְׁתּֽוּ׃

passages.text: So they will lack food and water; they will be appalled at the sight of one another wasting away in their iniquity.
passages.sermon:
God will take away their food and water.
The people will not have enough to eat or drink.
Each person will see his brother.
They will be shocked at what they see.
They will see each other wasting away.
Their sins will cause their bodies to waste away.
passages.original: לְמַ֥עַן יַחְסְר֖וּ לֶ֣חֶם וָמָ֑יִם וְנָשַׁ֙מּוּ֙ אִ֣ישׁ וְאָחִ֔יו וְנָמַ֖קּוּ בַּעֲוֺנָֽם׃פ
